issue: Calque: 'θα σε πάρω πίσω' mirrors English 'call back' and collides with παίρνω πίσω = take back / retract. Common in casual Athens speech but an anglicism; the native-cleaner verb is ξαναπαίρνω. Tip normalizes the calque by teaching 'take back'.

fix.target: Θα σε ξαναπάρω σε πέντε λεπτά.
fix.grammar: ξαναπαίρνω κάποιον (ksanapérno) = call someone back — cleaner than the anglicism 'παίρνω πίσω'.

issue: Same 'παίρνω πίσω' = call-back calque in the imperative ('Πάρε με πίσω'); ambiguous with 'take me back'. Native-cleaner: ξαναπάρε με / πάρε με.

Romanization drops the γχ nasal: ελέγχω is /eˈleɲço/ and the deck's own convention keeps the nasal (cf. el-1950 αγχώνομαι → 'anchónome'). 'elécho' is inconsistent and under-phonetic; should be 'eléncho'.

Tip misidentifies the referent: 'σίγουρος/σίγουρη matches the speaker's gender' is wrong. On this 2nd-person card the adjective agrees with the SUBJECT — the person addressed (a woman), not the speaker. As written it tells a learner σίγουρη marks the speaker's gender, contradicting the card itself.

fix.grammar: σίγουρος/σίγουρη (síguros/síguri) agrees with the person it describes — here 'you'.

issue: 'βοηθάει με το άγχος' reads as an English calque ('helps with'). Idiomatic Greek governs this with σε: βοηθάει στο άγχος (or κάνει καλό στο άγχος). The 'με' pattern is natural only with a person object (με βοηθάει με τα μαθηματικά).
